The Environmental Management Bureau Region 3 participated in the monitoring and evaluation activity conducted by the National Solid Waste Management Commission (NSWMC) to assess the implementation of the City Government of Cabanatuan’s approved 10-Year Solid Waste Management Plan.

During the two-day activity, the Bureau provided crucial technical and administrative support to the NSWMC team during coordination meetings and monitoring activities. Its participation helped ensure a thorough assessment of the City Government’s compliance with the objectives and strategies outlined in its Solid Waste Management Plan.

The City Government took the opportunity to showcase its achievements in environmental governance, presenting its legal instruments, programs and various awards recognizing its outstanding efforts in solid waste management. It also highlighted its operational facilities, projects and equipment used in managing solid waste, underscoring its continuing commitment to sustainable environmental practices.

Representatives from the Solid Waste Management Association of the Philippines, the Recycling, Composting/Resource Recovery and Processing Industry, and the Solid Waste Management Division of the EMB Central Office likewise joined the activity.

Under Section 5(c) of Republic Act No. 9003, or the “Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000,” the NSWMC is mandated to review and monitor the implementation of approved local solid waste management plans to ensure compliance and continuous improvement of waste management systems across the country.

Every November 2, we come together to remember our loved ones who have gone ahead of us. All Souls’ Day is not just a date on the calendar. It’s a moment to pause, reflect, and pray for those who once walked beside us and now rest in peace.

Here in the Philippines, this day holds a special place in our hearts. Families visit cemeteries, light candles, offer flowers, and say quiet prayers. For many, it’s also a time of reunion — sharing food, stories, and laughter as we keep the memory of our departed alive. This is what Undas is truly about; love that remains and remembrance that never fades

As we honor the souls of our loved ones, we’re reminded that death is not an ending, but a homecoming to God. The light of every candle we light is a symbol of faith, hope, and the promise of eternal life.

May today be a gentle reminder to hold our loved ones close — both here and in heaven — and to live each day with kindness, gratitude, and faith.
